selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveler understand from the oceans and rivers?
questions.answer: He understood that they give strong witness to the oneness and existence of Allah.

questions.question: About how much of the truths in the seas and rivers did the traveler see?
questions.answer: He saw only a very small part of them.

questions.question: How do the seas make their declaration according to the passage?
questions.answer: They declare it together, with great strength matching their vast size.

questions.question: Who are presented as witnesses supporting the testimony of the seas?
questions.answer: All the living creatures inside them.

questions.question: What main message is expressed in the statement about the seas and rivers?
questions.answer: That only Allah is truly worthy of worship and that creation points to Him.

questions.question: Which parts of nature are named together in this section as giving testimony?
questions.answer: The seas and the rivers, along with what they contain.

questions.question: What does the passage say the seas and rivers point to about Allah?
questions.answer: They point to the necessity of His existence and His unity.

questions.question: Which four broad signs are mentioned in the passage as being seen in seas and rivers?
questions.answer: Bringing things under control, preserving them, storing what is needed, and managing them.

questions.question: How is observation important in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage says these signs can be noticed in the world itself.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying these truths are observed?
questions.answer: It means they can be seen by paying attention to the world.

questions.question: What did the traveler notice after looking at the oceans and rivers?
questions.answer: He noticed that they contain many truths that affirm belief in Allah.

questions.question: Did the traveler think he had seen all of those truths or only a small amount?
questions.answer: Only a small amount.

questions.question: What are the seas described as saying together?
questions.answer: They are described as declaring that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: Why is the testimony of the seas described as powerful?
questions.answer: Because their witness matches their greatness and huge extent.

questions.question: Besides the seas themselves, what else supports this testimony?
questions.answer: Everything living in them supports it as evidence.

questions.question: What truth about Allah is emphasized by the words “Necessary Existent”?
questions.answer: That Allah’s existence is not dependent on anything else and must be true.

questions.question: What does the word “preservation” tell us about the creatures and contents of the waters?
questions.answer: It shows they are being protected and kept in order.

questions.question: What does “storing up” suggest in this passage?
questions.answer: It suggests that what is needed is kept ready in a planned way.

questions.question: What does “administration” mean here?
questions.answer: It means the waters and what is in them are governed and managed in an organized way.

questions.question: What kind of evidence is used in this passage: imagined ideas or signs that can be noticed?
questions.answer: Signs that can be noticed.

questions.question: In this section, what part of creation is the traveler reflecting on?
questions.answer: He is reflecting on the oceans and rivers.

questions.question: What did he realize about the truths found in them?
questions.answer: He realized that what he saw was only a tiny portion.

questions.question: What shared statement do the seas make in the passage?
questions.answer: They make a united statement of Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the seas are not giving weak evidence?
questions.answer: It says their testimony is strong and fits their enormous scale.
